# Protect trade secrets and confidential know-how

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When valuable confidential technical or commercial information requires a deliberate protection plan. An owned confidential-information register with practical access, sharing and departure controls.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Identify the information and business value

agent-runnable


Inventory the know-how, code, datasets, formulas, pricing or operating information to protect and who currently holds it. Distinguish public information, third-party confidential material and company-created information.

- Sources: [WIPO trade secrets](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/trade-secrets/index) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Choose the protection and sharing rules

human · human approval required


Counsel and business owners review ownership, confidentiality commitments and alternatives such as patenting or publication. Define permitted recipients and handling controls for each category without assuming a label alone establishes protection.

- Sources: [WIPO trade secrets](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/trade-secrets/index) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Implement approved access and storage controls

manual form/portal · human approval required · hard to undo


Authorized administrators restrict repositories, document stores and export paths to approved roles. Verify logging and recovery arrangements and keep secrets out of public tickets and general onboarding materials.

- Sources: [WIPO trade secrets](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/trade-secrets/index) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Review disclosures and train recipients

human · human approval required


Before sharing, verify the purpose, recipient authority and any required agreement. Explain handling and reporting expectations to staff and counterparties and retain evidence of approved disclosures.

- Sources: [WIPO trade secrets](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/trade-secrets/index) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Review access changes and suspected exposure

agent-runnable


Reconcile departures, role changes and external sharing with the register. Route suspected misuse to counsel and incident response, preserve evidence and reassess controls without making unsupported accusations.

- Verify: An owned confidential-information register with practical access, sharing and departure controls.
- Sources: [WIPO trade secrets](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/trade-secrets/index) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)
